questions.question: A woman has left-upper-quadrant pain, fever, and is unwell. She grows a gram-negative bacillus in both blood and urine cultures. It is a lactose fermenter with mucoid colonies and is indole-negative.
questions.question_raw: PM 3. Woman has left upper quadrant pain, fever, unwell. She grows GNB in both blood and urine cultures. It is a lactose fermenter with mucoid colonies. It is indole-negative.

parts.text: What are 4 other carbapenem-resistant enzymes that are clinically important?

parts_raw.text: What are 4 other carbapenem resistant enzymes that are clinically important (2)

questions.model_answer:
a) Klebsiella pneumoniae (lactose-fermenting, mucoid colonies, indole-negative; Escherichia coli would be indole-positive).
b) (1) KPC (2) NDM (3) VIM (4) IMP (also OXA-48, SME, GES).
questions.beyond_mandell: The named carbapenemase enzymes are from resistance literature (Mandell Ch. 18); this chapter identifies Klebsiella and notes it carries carbapenemases but does not list the enzyme families.

cohort_answer.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae (E. coli is indole positive). Other carbapenemases: NDM-1, KPC, VIM, IMP, SME, OXA-48, GES.
